---
title: "Copying a data.table with <- does not copy it"
ref: DT-02
categories: [data.table]
impact: silencieux
attendu: "`backup` unchanged, with column a only"
versions: "All versions of {data.table}"
source: "General R knowledge"
---

::: {.piege packages="data.table"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(data.table))

dt <- data.table(a = 1:2)
backup <- dt
dt[, b := a * 10]
backup

add_total <- function(d) {
  d[, total := 0]
  nrow(d)
}
add_total(backup)
names(dt)
```
:::

## Why

In R, `backup <- dt` copies nothing right away: both names point to the same object, and R only makes the copy when one of them is modified. But `:=` modifies the table **in place**, bypassing that mechanism. So both names see the new column.

The same goes inside a function: the argument `d` points to the caller's table, and `:=` modifies it, even though the function only returns a number.

## The fix

Make a real copy with `copy()` when you want to keep the original.

::: {.piege packages="data.table"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(data.table))

dt <- data.table(a = 1:2)
backup <- copy(dt)
dt[, b := a * 10]
backup
```
:::
